{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVQjccM8AAAABYf9eMw", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn3IfzhCETis", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn3If", "number": 7, "title": "Make the Rust/Wasm WonderSwan emulator play an original, redistributable homebrew game ROM", "body": "## Problem

The current browser app is a non-playable prototype: it selects WonderSwan / WonderSwan Color / SwanCrystal, stores local ROM bytes, and displays a blank Rust-owned framebuffer. It does **not execute cartridge instructions**, produce game graphics from emulated hardware, or respond to in-game controls.

The next milestone must be **genuinely playable in the browser**, not another ROM-loading mock-up. We also need a ROM that can be legally bundled, downloaded, and used for automated tests without distributing commercial games or requiring users to find copyrighted ROM dumps.

## Expected outcome

An unauthenticated visitor to **https://takahirox.github.io/wonderswan-rust/** can click **Play demo** (or an equivalently obvious action) and play a small **original WonderSwan homebrew game** running as a real ROM through the **from-scratch Rust emulation core compiled to WebAssembly**. The existing local ROM file picker must also be able to load and run the same compiled ROM file.

Minimum demo gameplay: a player-controlled object can be moved with documented controls; the player can reach or collect a target; the game visibly updates its score or progress; a win/completion state can be reached; and the game can be restarted and played again. Choose simple original visuals and a small game loop; do not spend the milestone on elaborate artwork, menus, or soundtrack.

The game must be **a real WonderSwan cartridge image** built from included original game source (not JavaScript that imitates gameplay, a special-case ROM identifier, precomputed frames, or a Rust-native reimplementation of the game). Its game logic must run through emulated CPU instructions and affect graphics/input via the emulated machine.

Retain all **three machine selections** with **SwanCrystal the default**. Design the demo for a **common hardware subset** so the same game can be played on WonderSwan (mono), WonderSwan Color, and SwanCrystal modes. Do not imply the three models are fully hardware-accurate merely because this demo works.

## Context and implementation scope

- Repository: `takahirox/wonderswan-rust`, `main`; builds via Cargo, `wasm-pack`, Vite and GitHub Pages. Follow [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/takahirox/wonderswan-rust/blob/main/AGENTS.md), [development flow](https://github.com/takahirox/wonderswan-rust/blob/main/docs/development-flow.md), [review guidelines](https://github.com/takahirox/wonderswan-rust/blob/main/docs/review-guidelines.md), and the repository Issue template. Author code guidance, documentation, Issues/PRs, and commits in English.
- Extend the existing `crates/ws-core`, `crates/ws-web`, and `web` components. Keep the emulation core browser-independent and use WebAssembly only as the adapter for the browser. Continue **implementing the emulator from scratch**: consult public hardware documentation but do not port, embed, or depend on an existing emulator core.
- Useful hardware reference: [WSdev Wiki](https://ws.nesdev.org/wiki/WSdev_Wiki), including [V30MZ CPU](https://ws.nesdev.org/wiki/NEC_V30MZ), [memory map](https://ws.nesdev.org/wiki/Memory_map), and [mapper](https://ws.nesdev.org/wiki/Mapper). Document the specific hardware behavior needed for the demo; do not assume a normal x86 executable can run unmodified as a WonderSwan cartridge.
- **CPU:** implement actual NEC V30MZ / 80186-compatible instruction fetch, decode, execute, registers, segment addressing, flags, stack/branches, memory reads/writes, and I/O as needed by the ROM. Instructions/flags and CPU state used by the game need deterministic unit tests. Unsupported cases should be explicit, not silently treated as NOPs.
- **Cartridge and startup:** parse/validate the required ROM format metadata, map the cartridge and memory banks into the WonderSwan address space, and enter executable code through a documented, firmware-free startup path. Do **not** commit any proprietary boot ROM/BIOS or copied firmware; document what boot-state approximation is used and its limitations.
- **Video:** make the 224 × 144 framebuffer reflect the game's hardware-generated state (at least the background/tile/sprite/palette subset used by the demo); do not substitute DOM/canvas-drawn game objects. Schedule CPU and video progression sufficiently to run the game at a consistent human-playable speed.
- **Input:** connect documented keyboard controls to emulated WonderSwan keypad I/O (and update game state through the ROM's reads of those inputs). Support starting/restarting the game and prevent the browser from scrolling on bound gameplay keys when appropriate. Optional Gamepad API support is not needed for this milestone.
- **Runtime/UI:** add start/run, pause/resume, and reset/restart behavior as needed for a reliable playable experience; keep model selection coherent, reset machine and game state when switching models, and handle ROM load/initialization errors without locking the interface. Use requestAnimationFrame or another suitable browser timing mechanism; avoid uncontrolled busy loops or excessive CPU use when idle or the tab is not visible.
- **Demo ROM:** add a genuinely original, redistributable, silent-if-convenient homebrew game in source form, plus a reproducible build recipe producing a valid `.ws` (or appropriate WonderSwan cartridge) ROM. Using an assembler/toolchain for the **homebrew ROM** is fine; do not use another emulator implementation. Commit or generate the demo binary for deployment and tests, with appropriate build instructions.
- **License and provenance:** explicitly license all original demo ROM source, binary, and graphics/audio assets under **CC0-1.0** (or another equally unambiguous freely redistributable permission documented in the repo). Record authorship/provenance and license coverage in a colocated notice/README; verify there are **no commercial ROMs, copied game assets, proprietary BIOS dumps, or unlicensed binaries**. If any third-party materials are proposed instead, independently verify their terms allow redistribution and document provenance; prefer wholly original assets.
- **Public accessibility:** bundle the authorized demo as a static site asset and expose a clearly labelled **Play demo** action. Keep manual local-file loading working without uploading users' ROMs. Maintain the existing GitHub Pages build-and-deploy-on-`main` workflow and production base path `/wonderswan-rust/`.
- **Project documentation:** update README with actual capabilities/limits, demo controls, how to launch/play the demo and load a local file, how to rebuild the ROM from source, how to validate it, and exact commands that work. Replace the blanket "games cannot play yet" notice with accurate limited-compatibility language only after real gameplay succeeds.

### Explicitly out of scope

Full commercial game compatibility; supporting every V30MZ undocumented instruction or cartridge mapper variant; hardware-perfect timing, LCD response emulation, EEPROM/RTC, save states, network play, gamepad support, a ROM catalog, a ROM-download service, and external BIOS support. **Sound is optional for this initial playable release** (a silent demo is acceptable). Those are follow-up work unless concretely required to execute the original demo.

The scope may be implemented in focused internal steps or reviewed through sub-PRs, but **do not close this Issue** on partial CPU scaffolding, simulated gameplay, or a display-only tech demo. The result must be playable end-to-end.

## Pre-merge acceptance criteria

- [ ] A redistributable **original** WonderSwan game ROM, its editable source, deterministic build instructions, and a clear license/provenance notice are included; the license permits anyone to play, copy, and redistribute the included ROM, source, and assets. A clean checkout can reproduce the game ROM (or follow a documented, runnable build process), and the generated ROM passes the project's ROM-format checks.
- [ ] The demo is a **real cartridge program** executed by the Rust CPU emulator, not a hardcoded special case or a JS/Rust mini-game outside the emulation path. ROM/CPU execution causes game graphics to change through emulated memory and video registers.
- [ ] The demo is **playable to completion** with keyboard input: move the player, interact with/collect a target, observe progress, reach the completion state, and restart. The same ROM works when manually selected via the existing file picker and when loaded via **Play demo**.
- [ ] The demo runs in **all three selectable models**, with SwanCrystal initially selected, and switching models resets ROM execution/input/frame state correctly. Any genuine model limitations are explicitly documented; no unsupported claim of full compatibility is made.
- [ ] The 224 × 144 framebuffer shows game graphics produced from emulated video state with repeatable frame progression (not the existing permanent black placeholder). Gameplay responds to real machine keypad emulation and does not rely on JS manipulating game position/score directly.
- [ ] CPU, memory-mapping, ROM-startup, input, and video mechanisms *used by the demo* have focused automated tests, including representative successful and error cases. Provide at least one integration test that loads the built demo ROM, executes machine steps/frames, asserts expected visible/framebuffer or machine-state changes, injects a button press, and verifies a resulting game-state change **through emulation**; no screenshots-only or mocks-only acceptance.
- [ ] The existing Rust workspace tests, formatting/Clippy, Wasm build, and frontend production build pass. The generated static site includes the original demo ROM and correct relative asset paths for `/wonderswan-rust/`.
- [ ] Run and **actually observe** an end-to-end browser smoke test on the pre-merge production preview: initialize Wasm, load bundled demo, play with controls, reach completion, restart, switch between all three models, and load the local demo ROM file. Record the steps and results; if a test could not be performed, report it as unperformed rather than claiming it passed.
- [ ] README and visible UI accurately state which ROMs/features are supported and that commercial-ROM compatibility remains incomplete. User-selected ROMs remain local to the browser; no unauthorized ROM or firmware is bundled.
- [ ] The implementation uses the existing architecture and minimal necessary tooling; no unrelated refactors, emulator dependencies, server infrastructure, or speculative subsystems are added.

## Optional validation

- Compare the homebrew game's behavior against genuine hardware (if available), without requiring physical hardware as a merge gate.
- Test on additional desktop/mobile browsers or with a second permissively licensed homebrew ROM **only after its license/redistribution terms are independently checked**. Additional game compatibility is informative, not mandatory for the first playable release.
- Evaluate nonessential audio support and broader CPU/PPU accuracy in separate follow-up Issues.

## Required post-merge verification

1. **Pending:** After merging into `main`, verify that the existing GitHub Pages workflow builds and publishes the new version; record the Actions run URL and final deployment result.
2. **Pending:** Open **https://takahirox.github.io/wonderswan-rust/** unauthenticated, click **Play demo**, play through to completion, and restart. Verify the bundled ROM, JS, and Wasm assets load successfully with no production-path errors, and that the same ROM can be selected via the file picker.
3. **Pending:** Confirm that the production page accurately describes the scope/compatibility and displays the demo's license/provenance link. Report any problems as follow-up work.

These live-publication checks happen after merge and must **not** be represented as passed or used as mandatory pre-merge approval gates.
